title: Mass Assignment - User Role Escalation via POST /api/v1/users
description: The POST /api/v1/users endpoint in the vulnerable API accepts a 'role' field in the request body via the createUserSchema Zod schema. The schema explicitly includes a 'role' field with enum ['ADMIN', 'BARBER', 'CUSTOMER'] and default 'CUSTOMER'. The handler extracts the role from the parsed request data and passes it directly to the createUser domain factory, which respects the provided role. This allows any authenticated user (including CUSTOMER) to create new users with arbitrary roles including ADMIN by simply including 'role': 'ADMIN' in the request body.
impact: Full privilege escalation. Any authenticated user (including CUSTOMER) can create new user accounts with ADMIN role, gaining full administrative access to the system. This is a critical privilege escalation vulnerability allowing complete system compromise.
mitigation: 1) Remove 'role' field from createUserSchema in the vulnerable API. 2) Set user role server-side based on authentication context (only ADMIN can create users with specific roles). 3) In the secure API, the createUserSchema excludes the 'role' field entirely and the handler sets the role server-side based on authentication context. The domain's createUser function should default role to 'CUSTOMER' for self-registration or require ADMIN context for role assignment.

history.details: Initial audit finding recorded for mass assignment in POST /api/v1/users
